title: Native harness — one Claude Code compatibility choice

steps.path: Only when Claude Code asks two questions with exactly the same wording
steps.headline: 22. Leave this Claude Code edge case unchanged, or block a submission that cannot preserve both answers?
steps.today: The approved native fix now keeps each question's answer separate. Claude Code uses a different answer format: it identifies questions by their wording, so two identical questions share one answer slot. Normal Claude Code cards with distinct wording are unaffected.
steps.problem: We cannot send two different answers for identical wording through that documented format. A worker added a warning and disabled Submit for this rare Claude Code case before asking you; that extra behavior is not yet approved or released.
steps.proposal: Keep the native fix either way. For Claude Code only, choose whether to preserve existing behavior or show an explicit limitation. Neither option adds a made-up answer format, secretly changes the questions, or claims the Claude Code duplicate case is fixed.

options.label: Native fix only
pros: Keeps this audit focused on the native harness and avoids an unapproved change to Claude Code cards.
Remove the new Claude Code warning and submission block; ordinary Claude Code behavior stays as before.
cons: The existing duplicate-wording limitation remains in Claude Code: independent answers cannot be faithfully returned.

options.label: Explain and block
pros: For duplicate wording only, the card explains why both answers cannot be submitted correctly.
Prevents a submission that silently collapses different answers into one.
cons: Submit is disabled for that Claude Code card. You must dismiss it and ask for differently worded questions.
This is an additional Claude Code interface change, not a complete fix for its answer format.
